DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 102 s. 2021 Aug. 09, 2021 MR. DANNY BOY ORILLA President, PAGLAOM Municipality of Pantukan Davao de Oro Dear Mr. Orilla: This has reference to your letter dated May 25, 2021 asking the Department's clarification on whether or not "SB accreditation" is necessary before PAGLAOM could be permitted by the Barangay to conduct an activity to give assistance to less fortunate people in terms of food, health and education, among others. In your subject letter, PAGLAOM, an acronym which stands for Pantukan Gays and Lesbian Organization Movement, is a duly existing and SEC-registered organization representing the LGBTQ+ sector in the Municipality of Pantukan, Davao de Oro. The goals of said organization include promoting gender equality as well as good health and hygiene; protecting the rights of the LGBTQ members and giving assistance to less fortunate people in terms of food, health and education, among others. On March 22, 2021, Mayor Roberto M. Yugo of the Municipality of Pantukan, Davao de Oro issued Executive Order No. 2021-020 entitled "AN EXECUTIVE ORDER AUTHORIZING THE BARANGAY CAPTAIN TO ISSUE CLEARANCE IN CONDUCTING MASS GATHERING WITHIN THEIR JURISDICTION" Meantime, on March 24, 2021, PAGLAOM sent a letter to Punong Barangay Thelma Yugo of Barangay Kingking, Pantukan, Davao de Oro asking permission to conduct an event, "Ayusin ko Buhok mo, Bigas mo Sagot Ko" wherein 100 beneficiaries from the said barangay can avail free haircut, hair treatment and a pack of rice on March 28, 2021, 8:OOAM at Cebuleda Gym. In response, PB Yugo asked PAGLAOM's "accreditation from the Sangguniang Bayan" and referred the latter's request to the Office of the Municipal Mayor of Pantukan. On March 30, 2021, the Office of the Mayor issued a letter requiring PAGLAOM to submit "accreditation issued by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Pantukan" and Organization Information such as names of officers, organization's objective and purpose and services offered. "Matino, Mahusat at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

On March 31, 2021, PAGLAOM sent a response and raised the point that "accreditation" from the Sangguniang Bayan is not required before an organization can conduct activities within the Barangay. On April 8, 2021 , the Office of the Mayor issued a letter stating that "the requirement of accreditation is to ensure that all organizations operating in Pantukan are not being used as fronts for recruitment of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People's Army and not for the representation in the local special body". It was also reiterated in the said letter that PAGLAOM is being required to submit an "accreditation issued by the Sangguniang Bayan ng Pantukan," among others, so that the Office of the Mayor can be referred to the proper authority for "background check". On April 15, 2021 , PAGLAOM reiterated that accreditation by the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) is not a prerequisite before an organization can conduct activities and added that Mayor Yugo himself personally administered the oath of office of the officers of PAGLAOM last November 8, 2020. Hence, the herein request of PAGLAOM. We are of the view that the requirement on SB accreditation shall be for purposes of proper accounting and representation in the local development councils only, not for the conduct of an activity within the Barangay or Municipality. Based on the given facts, it appears that the reason behind PAGLAOM's request to the Punong Barangay on March 24, 2021 was to seek the latter's permission in your conduct of an activity called "Ayusin ko Buhok mo, Bigas mo Sagot Ko" in Barangay Kingking. This "permission" relates to the issuance of barangay clearance which a barangay is authorized to issue under Section 152 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 for any activity conducted within its jurisdiction, thus: "SECTION 152. Scope of Taxing Powers. — xxxx (c) Barangay Clearance - No city or municipality may issue any license or permit for any business or activity unless a clearance is first obtained from the Barangay where such business or activity is located or conducted. For such clearance, the Sangguniang Barangay may impose a reasonable fee. The application for clearance shall be acted upon within seven (7) working days from the filing thereof. In the event that the clearance is not issued within the said period, the city or municipality may issue the said license or permit. Nowhere can we find in the aforequoted provision the requirement of SB accreditation before the barangay could issue the barangay clearance. Even as to the issuance of Mayor's permit, we also do not find the requirement SB accreditation, thus: "SECTION. 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — xxxx Page 2 of 4

(b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: xxxx (3) Initiate and maximize the generation of resources and revenues, and apply the same to the implementation of development plans, program objectives and priorities as provided for under Section 18 of this Code,particularly those resources and revenues programmed for agro-industrial development and country-wide growth and progress, and relative thereto, shall: (v) Issue permits. without need of approval therefor from any national Agency. for the holding of activities for any charitable or welfare purpose. excluding prohibited games of chance or shows contrary to law. public policy ane public morals;" (Emphasis Supplied) Rather, we find the requirement of SB accreditation under Section 108 of the same Code, thus: "SECTION 108. Representation of Non-Govemmental Organizations. - Within a period of sixty (60) days from the start of organization of local development councils, the nongovernmental organizations shall choose from among themselves their representatives to said councils. The local Sanggunian concerned shall accredit nongovernmental orqanizations subiect to such criteria as may be provided by law." (Emphasis Supplied) This representation in local development councils is the one contemplated under DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-72 entitled "GUIDELINES ON ACCREDITATION OF CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS AND SELECTION OF REPRESENTATIVES TO THE LOCAL SPECIAL BODIES." As to the concern of the Mayor that "the requirement of accreditation is to ensure that all organizations operating in Pantukan are not being used as fronts for recruitment of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People's Army and not for the representation in the local special body," he, as the local chief executive, can always require you to show him your SEC-registration certificate, list of activities to be undertaken during the activity, the recipients thereof, and the like. Also, the Mayor or the Punong Barangay could designate officials to man the place where the activity will be conducted to ensure that no illegal activities shall be undertaken. On a final note, it may be prudent to reiterate that Davao de Oro is under GCQ with heightened restrictions from August I to 15, 2021 which means that non-essential mass gatherings remain suspended. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
